A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GET, with matching methods, benchmarks and substantial shared results. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete supplementary material support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original GCD benchmark experiments, component ablations and supplementary analyses, including NEV and Clevr-4 results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds CUB comparisons of text-feature sources and TES mapping depths.

M1.justification: In Eq. (7), v2 changes the squared-distance contribution to TES's distillation loss from negative to positive. This revises the stated objective, while the two-stage architecture, CICO and visual-branch inference remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: v2 introduces WordNet names and CC3M captions as auxiliary retrieval data for the CUB comparisons in Section 5.3. The evaluated GCD datasets and tasks otherwise remain unchanged: ImageNet-R, NEV and Clevr-4 were already used in v1, including its supplements.

E2.justification: v2 Table 7 adds WordNet-based and CC3M-based retrieval, plus BLIP and BLIP-2 text generation, as alternatives to TES on CUB. The principal GCD comparator sets, including the supplementary PromptCAL-CLIP comparison, are retained.

E3.justification: New CUB experiments vary mapping depth from one to five layers and compare linear and MLP mappings. They also test replacing TES features with encoded retrieved or generated text under dual-branch training. Existing benchmark splits, ACC evaluation, training budgets and inference branch remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 5 adds mapping-depth and linear-versus-MLP sensitivity analysis to the existing token-count sweep. Table 7 additionally tests whether retrieving or generating explicit text can replace TES. The earlier loss-component ablations are retained within this expanded table.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages of three independent runs and the same main-result standard deviations, in v1 Table 7 and v2 Table 10. Both also report five-run Clevr-4 results. Moving the repeated-run statement into v2's main text does not introduce a new reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 Table 7 newly reports CUB All accuracies of 69.8, 72.3, 67.1 and 71.3 for WordNet, CC3M, BLIP and BLIP-2, respectively; TES remains at 77.0. Figure 5 adds depth-sweep results. Principal benchmark results match, while projector/adapter All scores from v1 Table 11 are omitted.

T1.justification: Eq. (7) substantively corrects the mathematical loss definition: v1's outer negative sign also negates the squared-distance term, whereas v2 adds that penalty positively. Other changes mainly clarify notation; no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about TES, multimodal dual-branch learning and state-of-the-art GCD performance remain. v2 highlights ImageNet-R generalization in its contribution list, but v1 Section 5.1 and Appendix A.1 already claim this contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation that inaccurate retrieved or generated text weakens discrimination for visually similar birds, and interprets the depth study as supporting a single linear mapping. The CLIP-exposure discussion and equal-modality-weighting limitation already appeared in v1's supplements and are largely relocated.

D1.justification: v2 documents retrieval-corpus sizes, cosine-similarity selection and the BLIP/BLIP-2 VQA prompt. Some existing detail is lost: v1 explicitly assigns lambda_h=2 and lambda_c=1, whereas v2 renames the entropy weight epsilon but says only that lambda_c is set to 2 and 1, respectively, leaving the assignment ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to WordNet, Conceptual Captions, BLIP and BLIP-2, and positions TES feature generation against text retrieval and generation. The existing related-work discussion and relationship to CLIP-GCD and SimGCD remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative by moving implementation details, pseudocode, CLIP discussion, backbone visualizations, qualitative analyses and limitations from the supplements into the main paper. It also revises introductory wording, reorganizes ablations, removes GET from the title and adds author biographies.

P2.justification: The main paper changes to a two-column journal layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of exhibits. Figure 1 is redrawn, the token plot gains a depth panel, and loss ablations merge into the expanded comparison table. v1's ImageNet-R histogram, TES-intuition schematic and detailed fine-tuning table are removed.

improvement.justification: The new CUB comparisons and depth study better support the choice of TES, while Eq. (7) now correctly penalizes embedding separation. These provide limited gains over an already extensive v1. Lost fine-tuning detail and the ambiguous loss-weight assignment partly offset the benefits; the principal empirical results and contributions remain unchanged.
